note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 92; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 28) on data/benches/hydrogen_volume.json: magnesium in hydrochloric acid, Mg + 2 HCl -> MgCl2 + H2, its hydrogen collected in a gas syringe: its molar volume and the gas constant.
title: Experiment: hydrogen's molar volume and R

steps.title: Your guess
steps.text: 0.050 g of magnesium ribbon (24.31 g/mol) gives one hydrogen molecule for each atom: 2.057 mmol. How many millilitres of gas will push the syringe out? Type your guess, then click "predict".
steps.why: A mole of any gas takes the same room at the same temperature and pressure (Avogadro).

steps.title: The magnesium into the acid
steps.text: Pick up the dish of magnesium, then right-click the flask. In the menu, click "tip in".

steps.title: The syringe on its mouth
steps.text: Quickly: pick up the syringe, right-click the flask, and click "on its mouth".
steps.why: Its nozzle in the flask's bung: the hydrogen the acid gives has nowhere to go but into the syringe, which it pushes out at the room's pressure.

steps.title: Collect it
steps.text: Watch the plunger move out as the magnesium fizzes away, its hydrogen stirring the acid round it. Speed up time if you like.
steps.why: The air in the flask is pushed into the syringe by the hydrogen made under it: the syringe reads what was made.

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.text: The reaction warmed the flask by several degrees, and its gas with it. Wait until the flask is back at the room's 20 C (speed up time if you like).
steps.why: Warm gas takes more room, and the water's vapour presses harder warm: read too soon and the volume reads high, by several millilitres.

steps.title: Read it
steps.text: Right-click the syringe and click "+ mL".
steps.why: Now the gas is at the room's temperature and pressure: its volume is what the moles take there.

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged

report.label: the gas collected
report.why: 2.057 mmol x 24.06 L/mol at 20 C and 101.3 kPa is 49.5 mL of hydrogen; it takes up water's vapour from the wet flask (2.34 kPa at 20 C), 1.2 mL more; and the syringe's ground plunger, pushed out by the warm gas, holds a millilitre or two out as it cools.

report.label: the molar volume
report.why: The hydrogen's own volume is the reading less its share of water's vapour, times (P - p_water) / P; over its moles. RT/P is 24.06 L/mol at 20 C and 101.3 kPa, the same for any gas.

report.label: R
report.why: R = PV / nT with the hydrogen's own pressure, 101.325 - 2.34 kPa, times the volume in mL, over the mmol and 293.15 K (kPa mL / mmol K is J / mol K).
